exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.matchNote: Exact movement match; library does not prescribe a different grip.
instructions: Take a seat at the chest-press machine and hold its handles with palms facing downward.
Adjust the setup to allow an appropriate pressing range.
Push the handles away, avoiding excessive elbow extension.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.matchNote: Flat bench confirmed by source description; our slug makes flat explicit.
instructions: Lie on a level bench, holding a dumbbell in either hand.
Position the weights beside your chest with palms directed toward your feet.
Brace your trunk and push both weights upward by straightening your arms.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Machine Pec Fly
exercises.matchNote: Selected handle-grip variant matches the document cues. Elbow-pad Machine Bent Arm Pec Fly is a separate variant, not an alias.
instructions: Set the seat so the grips sit at chest level; hold them with a small bend at the elbows.
Draw your hands toward each other, contracting your chest without changing the elbow bend.
Open your arms gradually, maintaining an upright chest.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Bench Press
exercises.matchNote: Source page confirms the corresponding bench-press variant; naming only.
instructions: Use an inclined bench with your feet supported on the floor and a dumbbell in either hand.
Lower the weights toward the sides of your chest.
Press the weights upward, extending your arms without forcing the elbows beyond straight.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.
instructionReviewNotes: Source quick steps and detailed text describe elbow lockout differently; summary avoids hyperextension.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.matchNote: Source page confirms the corresponding bench-press variant; naming only.
instructions: Lie on a level bench with feet supported on the floor; take the bar out of its supports.
Bend your elbows to bring the bar down toward your chest.
Push the bar upward, stopping before excessive elbow extension.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.
instructionReviewNotes: Source quick steps and detailed text describe elbow lockout differently; summary avoids hyperextension.

exercises.name: Cable Bench Chest Fly
instructions: Position a bench between the cable stacks and set the pulleys slightly lower than shoulder level.
Take a handle in either hand and center yourself between the cables.
Extend the handles forward, then open and close your arms while maintaining the elbow bend.
exercises.matchNote: User confirmed this candidate matches the intended seated supported fly. Page confirms bench/cable setup; seated equivalence accepted from user review.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise source paraphrase; user-confirmed movement match, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Machine Pulldown
exercises.matchNote: Source detailed explanation explicitly identifies the demonstrated variant as a wide overhand pulldown. Proposed slug uses cable resistance even though MuscleWiki calls it Machine Pulldown.
instructions: Secure your thighs beneath the pads and hold the bar with a wide, palms-forward grip.
Begin with arms extended; draw the bar toward your upper chest while keeping the pull controlled.
Allow the bar to rise gradually until your arms straighten again.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Machine Seated Cable Row
exercises.matchNote: Same seated cable-row movement; attachment is unspecified in the library and not frozen in the proposed slug.
instructions: Sit upright at the row station and take hold of the attachment.
Maintain a lifted chest while drawing the handles toward the sides of your abdomen.
Avoid changing your torso position as you complete the pull.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Narrow Pulldown
exercises.matchNote: User selected straight-bar narrow grip. The neutral alternative in the original label is not used; intermediate Neutral Pulldown stays separate.
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the pulldown station.
Sit holding the attachment, securing your thighs beneath the pads.
Draw the bar toward the collarbone, then guide it upward until your arms straighten.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched MuscleWiki page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Neutral Pulldown
exercises.matchNote: Neutral-grip movement matches. Original 10–15 degree lean remains a library setup note, not a separate source name. Distinct from the user-selected straight-bar Narrow Pulldown.
instructions: Fit a V-shaped handle and sit with your thighs secured by the pads.
Draw the attachment down toward the collarbone.
Return the attachment upward until the arms straighten.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Single Arm Row
exercises.matchNote: Movement and support match; source describes pulling toward chest, while library cues toward hip. Preserve the distinction for instruction review rather than altering the source name.
instructions: Hold one dumbbell and place the other hand on a stable bench for support.
Hinge until your trunk is approximately horizontal, keeping your abdomen braced.
Lift the dumbbell toward your torso with the working elbow close to your side.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Laying Incline Row
exercises.matchNote: User confirmed dumbbells. MuscleWiki specifies an incline of 30–45 degrees, covering the intended 30-degree setup. Original elbow-path cues stay separate.

Begin with the weights hanging below you, then draw your elbows backward and upward.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched MuscleWiki page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Machine Leg Press
exercises.matchNote: First of two explicit alternatives in the library; mapped separately rather than treating leg press and goblet squat as aliases.
instructions: Position your feet about shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Disengage the support and press the platform away without forcing the knees into lockout.
Bend your knees to lower the load while keeping your pelvis and lower back supported, then press upward again.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
exercises.matchNote: Second explicit alternative. Original cues specify a dumbbell at the chest.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell against the upper chest with elbows tucked and feet slightly wider than the shoulders.
Lower into a squat with your elbows tracking inside the knees.
Maintain a lifted chest as you push through your feet and stand again.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.matchNote: User confirmed seated. Reuses the same source movement as intermediate Seated Leg Curl; assign one exercise UUID at seeding, not one per level.
instructions: Set the seat and pads so the upper restraint secures the thighs and the lower roller rests near the Achilles area.
Use the handles to remain seated securely while bending your knees to curl the roller backward.
Straighten the knees again without forcing them past their normal end position.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.matchNote: Light is a load prescription, not a separate exercise identity.
instructions: Stand with feet approximately shoulder-width apart and the weights held in front.
Move your hips backward with only a modest knee bend, stopping when the hamstrings lengthen.
Bring your hips forward to regain an ordinary upright stance, without leaning backward.
exercises.instructionFormat: Concise paraphrase of matched source page, not verbatim text.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
exercises.matchNote: User confirmed dumbbell hip thrust for beginner entry. Exact source name/page previously verified; instruction collection pending resume.
instructions: Rest your upper back against a stable bench or box.
Plant both feet with heels down and toes facing forward.
Bend and extend through your hips, emphasizing a controlled contraction near the top.

Let your heels descend, pause briefly, then rise onto your toes.
Pause near the top and repeat with a controlled pace.
